label: PF Backlog 450
title: DEFECT: schedule/next returns executed items (implemented|verifying) -> worker re-executes
body:
Source: live dogfood run of the Stage 3c agent (2026-10-07), real PF API + real coordinator + real
wg-agent + real git worktree. NOT found by the stub e2e (the stub serves one item, so re-claim never showed).

DEFECT: `core/scheduler.py:263` lets `implemented` and `verifying` pass the status gate, so an item that has
already been executed is STILL returned by `schedule/next` and can be claimed and re-executed.

Evidence (live): the first dogfood run executed BI-DF-0001 and wrote back `verifying` (journal writeback
ok=true). The second run's `next_eligible` returned BI-DF-0001 again (not the fresh item), and the agent
re-claimed + re-executed it (marker showed BI-DF-0001). `scheduler.eligible(BI-DF-0001)` with status
`verifying` -> {ok: True, reasons: []}.

Root cause: `_ELIGIBLE_STATUSES = ("new","accepted","queued","scheduled")` (open, not yet executing) but the
gate also whitelists `implemented`/`verifying` (intended for a verification stage). The worker claim path
(`schedule/next` -> coordinator `/work`) is stage-agnostic, so ANY worker re-claims executed work. The only
thing preventing a double-claim is the coordinator lease - and once the run ends and the lease is released,
the item is claimable again in a non-terminal, already-executed status (infinite re-execution).

Impact: worker re-execution / duplicated work; the `executing -> implemented|verifying` post-run state is not
actually protected. Affects the WorkerGrid execution path (Stage 3c) and any consumer of schedule/next.

NOT affected: the coordinator lease (correct); the agent write-back (correct, ok=true).

Options (need a decision - touches PF-wide scheduling semantics):
  A. Stage filter on the worker claim path (recommended): keep `eligible()` as-is; make the EXECUTION claim
     ask only for not-yet-executed items (e.g. `stage=execute` / status allow-list on
     `GET /api/v1/engineering/schedule/next`), the coordinator passes it. Scoped; no change to existing
     consumers' default behaviour.
  B. Change the default: drop `implemented`/`verifying` from the eligible whitelist entirely (never
     claimable). Simple, but removes any verification-stage pickup and may surprise consumers.
  C. Record-only: track the defect, defer the fix.

dashboard_impact: needs_dashboard=false - backend scheduling correctness; no UI surface.
